name: authorized-keys-list carries the lines outside every rule, each with a reason
summary: admin.py authorized-keys-list reports, per line, whether it carries the kit's confinement options (restrict, or the four no-* options no-pty/no-port-forwarding/no-agent-forwarding/no-x11-forwarding; fields restrict, no_forwarding_options, confined_options; summary count without-confined-options) and its attention list carries the lines OUTSIDE every rule beside the stale-kit lines: unrestricted (the account's full shell - the operator's own key is normally exactly this on most installs, and the reason says so), other-command (another program or a shell, judged by what runs), this kit's command without restrict or the no-* options (port forwarding and a pty stay open), and a line serving another runtime - each with its reason in words in the notes. The project gate of endpoint.execute (key_project_refusal) is its first statement and execute is the only request-to-action path, pinned at the source.
